title: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Ltd - 543412 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Star Health Q4 FY26 underwriting profit rose to Rs 186 crore on a 95.7% combined ratio, but reported Q4 PAT was a Rs 55 crore loss on a Rs 558 crore MTM hit.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 GWP rose 17% YoY (N basis) to Rs 6,259 crore, with fresh retail growing 38% and the loss ratio improving to 65.2% from 69.2%. Full-year GWP crossed Rs 20,000 crore (Rs 20,369 crore, up 16%) and FY26 underwriting profit turned positive at Rs 206 crore versus a Rs 165 crore loss in FY25. Reported Q4 PAT was a Rs 55 crore loss against a Rs 271 crore profit a year earlier, driven by the equity-market MTM loss. Management introduced a normalised investment yield of 8%, under which FY26 PAT was Rs 1,222 crore (up 45%) and ROE 13.1%.

segments.name: Retail Health
segments.commentary: Fresh retail grew 38% YoY in Q4 and 37% for FY26 (N basis); retail policies grew 11% in Q4 and 8% for FY26. Market share was 31.3% in FY26; retail loss ratio 64.8% in Q4 and 68.2% for FY26.

segments.name: Group Health / SME
segments.commentary: Management said SME was 78% of group business in FY26 versus 58% in FY25, with a recalibrated strategy that drove the group loss ratio improvement. No explicit group GWP figure was given.

guidance_outlook: Management targets sustainable high-teen growth and mid-to-high-teen ROE.
Annual price increases will continue across all products; management said no change beyond normal pricing is foreseen, and about 80% of the book is to be repriced from Q4 FY26 through Q1 FY27.
Reporting moves to 1/n basis for business and growth from FY27.
NEP growth is expected to lag GWP growth because of long-term policy sales, with catch-up expected in coming quarters.
Management expects the long-term share of NEP to keep rising next year.
Agent network to reach 1 million in two years, adding about 1 lakh agents a year.
capex_capacity: Home Healthcare, telemedicine and condition management usage rose 4-5x over the year, with Q4 consumption up about 9x. FY26 included over 90,000 telemedicine calls and over 40,000 pure telemedicine calls.
Claims platform migration to the Medi Assist platform is nearly complete, with the last product set to shift by Q1 FY27 end.
Customer app has over 14 million downloads and more than 1.5 million monthly active users; 95% of fresh premium is collected digitally.
demand_pricing: Retail Health premiums grew 30.2% YoY in H2 FY26 versus 11.2% for non-life. For full FY26, retail health grew close to 20% and non-life 9.3%.
New-to-insurance share of fresh premium was 94% in Q4 (90% a year earlier) and 93% for FY26 (89% in FY25).
Volume retention improved 1-1.5% YoY; the company cited about 86-87% volume retention and a renewal ratio of 99%. GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps and NOP-based 100 bps.
Agent productivity rose about 37% on fresh and 18% on total business. Over 90% of retail comes from agency and D2C channels.
Senior citizens are about 20% of the portfolio; the senior citizen commission reduction took effect April 2024 (FY25) and drove part of the commission ratio gain.
Long-term vs annual NEP split is about 80:20, moving 100-150 bps toward long-term on premium basis.

qa_highlights.question: How will the retail loss ratio (about 68%) get back to 65-66% levels seen in FY23-24, and how will seasonal vector-borne claims be handled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said frequency and severity were managed in the high-single digits for FY26 and that Q4 benefited from lower frequency. It cited telemedicine and home healthcare usage growth and repricing of about 80% of the book from Q4 FY26 to Q1 FY27, but gave no numerical target.

qa_highlights.question: Why is retail growth lagging the industry, and how should the gap evolve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it prioritises quality and profitable geographies over market share. Its market share was 31.3% in FY26, growth on N basis was 39% for FY26, and the company is not chasing share at the cost of profit.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the loss ratio improvement: renewal book, new business, severity or fraud controls?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gain is a sum of parts: renewal repricing, sourcing quality, geography selection, and fraud, waste and abuse controls. Q4 frequency improvement cut across the whole book.

qa_highlights.question: Is the retention ratio uptick linked to long-term policies?
qa_highlights.answer: The CFO attributed the Q3/Q4 retention noise to renewals pulled into September after the GST cut, with some spillover into Q1. Volume retention improved 1-1.5% for the year.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a need for a major repricing in FY27, and is the current price rise enough for the target combined ratio?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no need for above-normal increases. It expects the current annual pricing strategy to be sufficient to hit the target combined ratio.

qa_highlights.question: How is Bima Sugam expected to affect sourcing and renewals?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Bima Sugam is a consumer platform for affordable plans, that it will not be zero-cost, and that Star Health is a shareholder and supportive of it.

qa_highlights.question: Did the GST cut lift renewals and sum insured?
qa_highlights.answer: Himanshu Walia said GWP-based renewal retention rose 300 bps, with customers opting for higher sum insured and riders, and that distributor income had risen over 50% since the GST announcement.

qa_highlights.question: Management did not answer on the EoM regulation's treatment of non-compliant companies and declined to comment on it, saying IRDAI guidance on EoM is awaited.

risks_watch: Retail loss ratio is still about 68% for FY26 versus the 65-66% seen in FY23-24; sustainability of the Q4 frequency improvement across a full cycle is unproven.
Equity-market volatility: Rs 558 crore Q4 MTM loss turned reported Q4 PAT negative; the normalised 8% yield is a new reporting basis.
NEP growth lagging GWP growth due to long-term policy sales; deferred revenue quantum was not disclosed and will be shared offline.
Pending IRDAI EoM / commission guidance and the Bima Sugam rollout could change distribution economics.
Growth gap versus industry retail growth (about 19% vs about 29% in Q4, per an analyst) persists; the company is prioritising profitable cohorts.
Group Health volume is being deliberately reduced; the SME mix is rising.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the loss ratio and underwriting turnaround, with specific metrics given throughout. Evasive on EoM regulation (declined to answer) and on the retail growth gap versus the industry, which was framed around profitability rather than share.
key_quotes: We are not so much focused on the portability side of business.
So, we are not desperate to grow our market share at the cost of profits.
It's a sum of all parts, right? It's not one can lay a finger on any one particular item.
We are probably the only company in this space operating within the current guidelines.

growth.why: Management targets sustainable high-teen growth, backed by ~20% retail health growth in FY26, 38% fresh retail growth in Q4, about 80% of book repriced through Q1 FY27, and a stated agent network target of 1 million in two years; no specific capacity additions were given.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q4 FY26 loss ratio fell to 65.2% from 69.2% and combined ratio to 95.7% from 98.4%, with about 80% of the book repriced from Q4 FY26 through Q1 FY27 and FY26 expense ratio improved 30 bps to 30.1%.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management targets sustainable high-teen growth after FY26 GWP grew 16% to Rs 20,369 crore and fresh retail grew 38% in Q4, with agent network to reach 1 million in two years (about 1 lakh added a year).

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided only to sustainable high-teen growth and mid-to-high-teen ROE, held rather than raised, and said no above-normal repricing is needed in FY27.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Retail loss ratio is still 68.2% for FY26 versus 65-66% in FY23-24, Q4 frequency gain is unproven across a full cycle, and equity MTM swings drove a Rs 558 crore Q4 hit.

rows.label: IRDAI EoM and Bima Sugam distribution impact
rows.why: EoM guidance is awaited and management declined to comment on treatment of non-compliant companies, while Bima Sugam will not be zero-cost and could change distribution economics.

rows.label: Annual repricing of about 80% of book
rows.why: About 80% of the book is repriced in this window and management expects the current annual pricing to hit the target combined ratio, with the retail loss ratio at 68.2% for FY26.

rows.label: NEP lag from long-term policy sales
rows.why: NEP growth is expected to lag GWP growth as long-term policies (about 80:20 long-term vs annual) defer revenue, with catch-up expected in coming quarters; deferred quantum not disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the loss ratio, underwriting turnaround and repricing, but cautious on EoM regulation (declined to answer) and deflected on the retail growth gap versus industry; analysts pushed on retail loss ratio sustainability and growth lag.
